transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

My team keeps telling me my behavior and decisions don’t make sense anymore, and I feel like I can’t control what I’m doing at work. It has gotten to the point where my spouse and our HR director persuaded me to come here because they are so worried about how I'm running things.
Have you ever had a similar period before when you felt unusually energized, needed less sleep, or acted impulsively for days or longer? Or is this the first time this has ever happened?

No, I’ve never experienced periods where I felt unusually energized, needed less sleep, or acted impulsively like that. This is definitely the first time I’ve ever gone through a decline and disorganization like this.
Before these changes started, did you have any recent medical illness, head injury, seizure, new medication, or use of alcohol or drugs? Also, when did these behavior changes begin?

No, I didn't have any medical illnesses, head injuries, seizures, or history of drug or alcohol use before this. The changes in my behavior and the decline in my functioning actually started a little over two years ago, right around the time of a very stressful merger project at work.
Since these changes began, have you had any memory problems, trouble finding words, getting lost, or other changes in thinking or personality? Have family or coworkers noticed those changes too?

Yes, my thinking has felt completely different—I constantly lose track of strategic documents and feel emotionally flat and blank. My spouse, colleagues, and the board have definitely noticed, and they are highly alarmed by my erratic decisions and unexplained absences. It's a massive shift from how I used to be, and it's why they pushed me to get help.

Have you also had progressive problems with language or understanding words, trouble recognizing familiar people or places, or difficulty performing everyday tasks you used to do easily? Or do your symptoms feel more like a persistent change in mood, such as ongoing sadness, irritability, or loss of interest?

No, I don't have trouble recognizing people or understanding language, but I have experienced a profound loss of interest and struggle with daily tasks. I feel completely flat and blank rather than sad, often sitting for long stretches doing nothing at all. I've lost all joy in my art projects and even struggle with basic routines like showering or yoga.

Have your memory and thinking problems steadily worsened over the past two years even when your mood felt unchanged, or do they mostly happen only when you feel flat and uninterested? Also, have others noticed clear progressive decline in your judgment or daily functioning separate from your mood?

Yes, this slide in my thinking and decision-making has been a steady, progressive decline over the last two years, persisting regardless of my mood. My spouse, the board, and HR have definitely noticed this decline, pointing out my erratic decisions, missed meetings, and how much I struggle with basic daily routines.

Have you been formally diagnosed with Alzheimer’s disease or another dementia, or has a doctor told you that your memory and thinking problems are due to a neurodegenerative condition? If so, did the flat mood and loss of interest begin only after those cognitive problems started?

No, I have never been diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease, dementia, or any other neurodegenerative condition. I am only now seeking a psychiatric evaluation to figure out what is causing these symptoms.
Have you had any brain or neurologic evaluation for this progressive decline, such as memory testing, a neurologist visit, or a brain MRI/CT scan? If yes, what were you told?

No, I haven't had any neurological evaluations, memory testing, or brain scans like an MRI or CT scan yet. Seeing a psychiatrist is the very first formal step I am taking to figure out what is going on.

Have you developed any new neurological symptoms over these two years, like tremor, stiffness, balance problems, falls, weakness, numbness, or changes in bladder control? Or has it mainly been a gradual change in motivation, judgment, and thinking without those physical symptoms?

No, I haven't experienced any of those physical symptoms like tremors, stiffness, weakness, or balance issues. It has really just been a gradual, frustrating slide in my motivation, judgment, and thinking over the last two years. I feel completely flat and blank, and I've become unable to manage my usual responsibilities.

Over these two years, have you had fixed false beliefs or heard/seen things other people did not, such as thinking coworkers were plotting against you? If yes, did those experiences begin before or after the decline in your judgment and motivation?

I haven't had beliefs about coworkers plotting against me, but for the last three months, I've regularly heard a man's voice—like someone on a conference call—commenting on my actions and criticizing me. This voice started much later, whereas my decline in motivation and judgment began about two years ago.

Before the voice started, did you spend most days feeling depressed or hopeless, or was the main problem a gradual worsening of your judgment, motivation, and thinking even without feeling sad? Which came first and was more prominent?

The gradual worsening of my motivation, thinking, and judgment definitely came first and was much more prominent, starting over two years ago. I didn't feel particularly sad or depressed, but rather completely flat, blank, and devoid of my usual drive. The voice only started about three months ago, long after this slide had already taken over.

Has anyone close to you noticed a clear change in your personality or social behavior—such as becoming disinhibited, apathetic, losing empathy, or acting compulsively—progressively over these two years? If so, can you give one example?

Yes, my spouse, HR, and the board have all noticed major changes and are deeply concerned. I've become completely flat and apathetic, pulling away from my friends and the art projects I used to love. I also act erratically at work now, sometimes snapping at my colleagues or laughing at completely inappropriate moments without knowing why.

Has any doctor ever suggested frontotemporal dementia, Pick’s disease, or another specific brain disease to explain these personality changes? Also, does anyone in your family have a history of early dementia or major personality change?

No, no doctor has ever suggested frontotemporal dementia, Pick's disease, or any other brain disease to me. I'm also not aware of anyone in my family having a history of early dementia or major personality changes.
